answer: Sybil resistance via quadratic cost for identity multiplicity. Buying N fake identities costs N squared in bonded stakes, so one actor can't cheaply flood the network. Each identity is pinned to a single 'island' of peer-shard; cross-shard attestation flows only through a narrow 'bridge' that tracks how much fresh weight a shard contributes, throttling sudden influxes. A 'quartz' clock, derived from emission hashes, forces staggered stake maturation so mass-spawned identities can't unlock together. Attacker cost: quadratic bonds plus sequential time gates.
